title: Incident Playbook: Tiered Recovery & Capacity Fallback Matrix
author: Marcus Lee
body:
Summary:
This playbook defines a compact, decision-oriented approach to handling SLO violations, capacity stress, and progressive recovery for Redwood's inference platform. It combines: a) a clear SLO/error-budget taxonomy, b) an executable capacity fallback matrix, c) incident escalation and retrospective triggers, and d) operational tooling integrations for automation and observability.

Scope:
- Services covered: serving-runtime, model-router, ingress-gateway, kv-cache, telemetry-pipeline, capacity-orchestrator.
- Applies to hosted, dedicated, and private fleets where Redwood controls autoscaling and routing.
- Excludes non-LLM control plane services (billing pipeline, payroll).

Objectives:
- Keep p99 token latency and availability SLOs within targets while minimizing cost and user-facing failures.
- Provide deterministic, auditable actions for progressive degradation and recovery.
- Ensure incident review requirements scale with severity and SLO impact.

SLO & Error Budget Taxonomy (quick reference):
- Critical SLOs:
  - Availability: 99.95% (monthly) for control-plane endpoints, 99.9% for tenant inference endpoints (tier-dependent).
  - p99 generation latency: <= 500ms for small models, <= 1200ms for long-context models as defined per model-profile.
- Error budget windows: rolling 30d for availability; rolling 7d for latency-sensitive production routes.
- Burn-rate levels (7d window):
  - Green: burn_rate <= 1x (no automated mitigation)
  - Amber: 1x < burn_rate <= 4x (automated mitigations triggered)
  - Red: burn_rate > 4x (escalation to oncall + capacity fallback)

Tiered Capacity Fallback Matrix (decision table):
- Inputs evaluated every 60s by capacity-orchestrator: current burn rate, cluster utilization, queue length, p95/p99 latency delta, model compatibility set.

| Tier | Trigger condition | Automated actions (order) | Human action | Notes |
|------|-------------------|--------------------------|--------------|-------|
| Tier 0 (Normal) | burn_rate in Green; utilization < 70% | None (observe) | N/A | Normal ops. |
| Tier 1 (Moderate) | Amber burn_rate OR utilization 70-85% | 1) Activate prefix KV cache eviction policy; 2) Enable request coalescing for identical prompts; 3) Increase per-replica concurrency (if safe) | Notify oncall channel; assess traffic profile | Apply conservative cost caps. |
| Tier 2 (High) | Red burn_rate OR utilization 85-95% OR sustained p99 > target *1.2 | 1) Route new low-priority tenants to cheaper model-variants; 2) Autoscale add warm-pool nodes (best-effort preemptible + reserved); 3) Throttle background rerank/embeddings jobs; 4) Increase batching window to 50ms | Pager to SRE primary; run capacity checklist | Metric gating prevents cascading. |
| Tier 3 (Critical) | utilization > 95% OR catastrophic model-serving failure | 1) Global routing fallback to smaller model family for public routes; 2) Reject new long-context requests with 413 + client hint; 3) Emergency divert to dedicated spare-region; 4) Trigger purchase/burst contract (if configured) | Full incident war room; exec notify | Trigger incident review with highest severity. |

Decision flow (condensed):
1) Telemetry detects burn_rate > 1x for 15m -> mark Amber.
2) Amber sustained 30m or all model partitions show latency delta -> apply Tier 1 automated actions.
3) If Amber escalates to Red or utilization thresholds hit -> apply Tier 2.
4) For catastrophic component failure (node-pool OOM, kernel failure) -> immediate Tier 3.

Operational Tooling Integrations (implementation):
- telemetry-pipeline: emits s.lo_burn, p95/p99, queue_depth, per-tenant request rates to metrics cluster.
- capacity-orchestrator: reads metrics and posts decisions to router/api for routing/scale changes.
- error-budget-orchestrator: owns burn-rate calculation and triggers webhooks.
- runbook-runner: executes pre-approved actions (cache toggles, reroute, throttle) as idempotent jobs.

Sample automation webhook payload (JSON):
{
  "event": "capacity_fallback",
  "service": "serving-runtime",
  "tier": "2",
  "reason": "burn_rate:5.3,util:88%",
  "actions": ["route-low-priority-to-variant:small-v2", "scale:warm_pool:+8"]
}

Runbook: Tier 2 recovery checklist (executable steps):
1) Confirm alert details (metrics window, affected partitions, top-10 tenants by QPS).
2) Execute automated fallback (runbook-runner job idempotent-run-<ts>).
3) Validate that p95 improved within 5 minutes. If not:
   a) Rollback increased batching; b) Verify KV cache hit-rate; c) Check per-model memory pressure logs (/var/log/serving/*).
4) Inform product owners and SRE lead with impact summary.
5) If Tier 2 persists 30m -> escalate to Tier 3 and open incident channel.

Incident Severity & Postmortem Requirements:
- Sev3 (Tier 1): Document incident summary and mitigation within 72 hours; no formal postmortem required unless customer impact > 1% of tenant base.
- Sev2 (Tier 2): Full postmortem required; include timeline, contributing factors, runbook gaps, and a remediation plan with owner and ETA.
- Sev1 (Tier 3): Immediate incident review within 48 hours; executive summary within 24 hours; full postmortem and blameless RCA with mitigation tickets entered in backlog within 7 days.

Incident Review Standards (evidence checklist):
- Required artifacts for postmortem: metrics dashboards (60m window pre/post), service logs filtered by trace-id, capacity-orchestrator decision log, error-budget-orchestrator webhook history, runbook-runner job records, and customer-facing status updates.
- Postmortem template fields: summary, impact, root cause analysis, timeline, detection & mitigation, why-not/why-did-not-mitigate, corrective actions, validation plan.
- Evidence retention: attach telemetry snapshots (raw) and logs to the postmortem page; store in confluence attachments for 90 days minimum.

Capacity Planning Guidance (practical knobs):
- Headroom policy: maintain 20% free capacity headroom at monthly 99th percentile traffic.
- Warm pools: maintain warm pool equal to 10% of steady-state replicas per region. Warm pool should be heterogenous across instance families to avoid simultaneous preemption.
- Autoscale limits: per-cluster max_scale set by cost tier; critical customers may have dedicated quotas.
- Preemption strategy: preemptible nodes used for background embeddings/low-priority traffic only; blocklist critical routes.

Quality Gates & Rollouts:
- New model rollouts require a canary at 5% traffic for 24h and SLO observability. If canary impacts error budget burn > 2x baseline -> automatic rollback to previous version.
- Traffic shaping config stored in git (config repo: infra/traffic-shaping). Changes must pass CI sim tests.

Playbook examples (CLI snippets):
- Force-enable request coalescing for model family small-v2:
  curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://control-plane/api/v1/ops/coalesce -d '{"model_family":"small-v2","enable":true}'

- Trigger warm pool scale:
  rdctl cluster scale --region us-west2 --pool warm --delta 8 --reason "autofallback-tier2"

Ownership & RACI (short):
- Detection & instrumentation: Observability team (primary), SRE (secondary).
- Automated fallback policies: SRE platform (primary), Serving runtime (secondary).
- Incident reviews & postmortems: SRE (primary), Product & Model Ops (reviewers).

Runbook Maintenance & Governance:
- Runbooks and the capacity matrix are reviewed quarterly during the SRE reliability sync.
- Any automated action that performs a write to control-plane must have a two-person approval and an undo action defined.

Validation & Continuous Improvement:
- Quarterly chaos drills must include one scenario that validates the Tier 2 -> Tier 3 escalation path.
- Maintain a small suite of synthetic prompts per traffic class to measure p99 across model variants; baseline daily and surface regressions in the reliability dashboard.

Appendix A: Example metrics thresholds (for reference):
- p95 latency delta threshold: 1.15x baseline.
- queue_depth threshold per-replica: 250 concurrent in-flight tokens.
- KV cache hit-rate target: >= 75% under steady state.
- acceptable background job throttle: up to 90% reduction for low-priority embeddings.

Appendix B: Contact list (oncall rota):

- SRE secondary: @sre-secondary
